title: Self-stabilization at the edge of stability
statement: Prove that gradient descent with step size eta on a two-layer network (beyond the quadratic-model setting) drives the top Hessian eigenvalue to 2/eta and keeps it there while the loss decreases non-monotonically.
anchors_from_memory: Cohen et al. 2021; Damian, Nichani, Lee 2023 (self-stabilization under assumptions)
litcheck: KEEP: 2610.23007 (two-neuron ReLU, 1D data) is a minimal case; two-layer networks in general open (13 Nov)

title: Clustering of tokens in self-attention dynamics
statement: For the continuous-time self-attention dynamics on the sphere with V = identity (Geshkovski, Letrouit, Polyanskiy, Rigollet), prove that for every inverse temperature beta and dimension d >= 3 and almost every initial configuration the tokens converge to a single cluster.
anchors_from_memory: Geshkovski-Letrouit-Polyanskiy-Rigollet, A mathematical perspective on transformers, open problems
litcheck: DROP: answered: Markdahl et al. 2018 (d>=3, connected graph, increasing convex phi synchronizes) covers phi=e^{beta t} for every beta; see Criscitiello-Rebjock-McRae-Boumal 2405.18273 (13 Nov)

title: The leap complexity conjecture
statement: Prove that online SGD on a two-layer network learns a sparse function on the hypercube with Theta(d^{max(Leap-1,1)}) samples, Leap being the leap complexity of its Fourier support, for jointly trained layers.
anchors_from_memory: Abbe, Boix-Adsera, Misiakiewicz 2023 (proved for layerwise training)
litcheck: KEEP: Abbe-Boix-Adsera-Misiakiewicz 2302.11055 prove it for layerwise training; jointly trained open (13 Nov)

title: Depth separation between depth three and depth four
statement: Is there a function on [0,1]^d computable by polynomial-size depth-4 ReLU networks that polynomial-size depth-3 networks cannot approximate in L2 under a natural distribution?
litcheck: KEEP: 2610.28800 separates depth 2 from 3 under Gaussian measure; 3 vs 4 open (13 Nov)

title: Provable grokking on modular addition
statement: Prove that gradient descent with weight decay on a two-layer network trained on a fraction of modular addition first interpolates and only after a time growing with 1/lambda generalizes, with the learned Fourier features.
anchors_from_memory: Nanda et al. 2023; Mohamadi et al. 2024; Morwani et al. 2024
litcheck: KEEP: 2609.26679 (homogeneous nets, squared loss) and 2610.22593 are partial; the modular-addition statement with Fourier features open (13 Nov)

title: Global convergence of gradient descent for deep ReLU networks at moderate width
statement: Prove that gradient descent from random initialization reaches zero training loss for depth >= 3 ReLU networks whose width is polynomial in n but below the neural-tangent-kernel regime.
anchors_from_memory: Allen-Zhu-Li-Song; Du et al.; Nguyen-Mondelli; Bombari-Amani-Mondelli (minimum width)
litcheck: KEEP: no hit in the query; NTK-width results only (13 Nov)

title: Benign overfitting of gradient-trained two-layer ReLU networks
statement: Characterise the data distributions for which GD-trained two-layer ReLU networks interpolate noisy labels and still have test error tending to the Bayes error, beyond near-orthogonal high-dimensional data.
anchors_from_memory: Frei, Chatterji, Bartlett 2022; Kou et al. 2023; Kornowski-Yehudai-Shamir 2023 (tempered)
litcheck: KEEP: results need near-orthogonal or moderate-dimension data (2403.06903, 2505.16204) (13 Nov)

title: Convergence of Adam with problem-independent hyperparameters
statement: Does Adam with fixed beta1 < sqrt(beta2) < 1 independent of the problem converge to stationary points on smooth nonconvex objectives, or is there a counterexample?
anchors_from_memory: Reddi et al. 2018; Zhang et al. 2022 (problem-dependent beta2); Wang et al. 2023
litcheck: DROP: answered in the stochastic setting: Reddi-Kale-Kumar 1904.09237 Thm 3 gives divergence for every fixed beta1<sqrt(beta2) (13 Nov)

title: The catapult phase for wide networks
statement: Prove the catapult dynamics of Lewkowycz et al. (loss spike then convergence to a flatter region for step sizes between 2/lambda0 and 4/lambda0) for two-layer networks of finite width with non-linear activations.
anchors_from_memory: Lewkowycz et al. 2020; Zhu et al. 2023 (quadratic models)
litcheck: KEEP: only quadratic models and empirical work (2301.07737, 2306.04815) (13 Nov)

title: Optimal step count for score-based diffusion
statement: What is the optimal dimension dependence of the number of discretisation steps for diffusion models to reach KL error eps with L2-accurate scores and finite second moment: linear in d (Benton et al.), or sqrt(d), or smaller?
anchors_from_memory: Benton, De Bortoli, Doucet, Deligiannidis 2024; Chen et al. 2023; Li et al. 2024
litcheck: KEEP: upper bounds only; the optimal dimension dependence (lower bound) open (13 Nov)

title: Neural collapse in deep networks trained on data
statement: Prove that gradient descent on cross-entropy for a deep network (not the unconstrained-features model) on separable data reaches neural collapse of the last-layer features.
anchors_from_memory: Papyan-Han-Donoho 2020; Mixon et al.; Sukenik-Mondelli-Lampert 2023 (deep UFM)
litcheck: KEEP: 2410.04887 shows collapse at weight-decay optima of wide networks, 2510.21078 shallow; GD on deep networks open (13 Nov)

title: Minimal width for uniform universal approximation by ReLU networks
statement: Determine the exact minimal width of deep ReLU networks that are dense in C(K, R^{d_y}) for compact K in R^{d_x}.
litcheck: KEEP: 2309.10402 settles L^p width max(dx,dy,2) and a uniform lower bound d_y+1; the exact uniform width open (13 Nov)

title: In-context learning of nonlinear functions by trained transformers
statement: For a one-layer softmax transformer trained by gradient flow on in-context regression with a nonlinear function class (e.g. single-index), characterise the in-context predictor it converges to.
litcheck: KEEP: linear and specific nonlinear classes only; general characterisation open (13 Nov)

title: Implicit bias of gradient descent in deep matrix factorization
statement: Give an explicit characterisation of the limit of gradient flow from small initialization on depth-L matrix factorization for matrix completion, now that it is not nuclear-norm minimisation.
anchors_from_memory: Gunasekar et al. 2017; Razin-Cohen 2020; Li-Luo-Lyu 2021 (greedy low-rank learning)
litcheck: KEEP: no hit; Razin-Cohen show it is not a norm; no explicit characterisation known (13 Nov)

title: Sample complexity of learning parities with transformers by gradient descent
statement: Prove a lower bound on the samples or steps gradient descent needs for a constant-depth transformer to learn k-sparse parities without intermediate tokens, matching the known upper bounds.
anchors_from_memory: Edelman et al. 2022; Kim-Suzuki 2025; related to N03 (CoT S_5)
litcheck: DROP: near-duplicate of replacement N03 (S_5 chain-of-thought separation, gradient lower bound) (13 Nov)

title: Mean-field limit of deep residual networks
statement: Prove a mean-field limit (law of large numbers in width and depth) for the training dynamics of deep residual networks and the global convergence of the limit.
litcheck: DROP: Barboni-Peyre-Vialard 2403.12887 and earlier mean-field ResNet work cover much of it; statement too loose to vet (13 Nov)

title: Sharpness of SGD minima under label noise
statement: Prove that SGD with label noise on an overparametrised network converges to a minimiser of the Hessian trace on the zero-loss manifold, with a rate, beyond the small-learning-rate limit.
litcheck: DROP: Damian-Ma-Lee 2021 prove label-noise SGD reaches stationary points of the trace-regularised loss with a rate; remaining gap too loose (13 Nov)

title: Width-depth trade-off for exact ReLU representation
statement: Restating N01: determine the minimal width of a depth-k ReLU network that exactly represents every continuous piecewise-linear function on R^d with a given number of pieces.
litcheck: KEEP: 2610.26795 is a depth construction for max; the exact width-depth trade-off open (13 Nov)
